claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin coating on a conventional metal substrate without nano-CeO2.
Nano-CeO2 particles will be added to the alloy powder feed while other deposition conditions are held constant.
Adding nano-CeO2 to the FeNiCrCoCu coating refines its grain structure.
Adding nano-CeO2 produces enhanced, continuous Ce-enriched oxide films at grain boundaries.
Nano-CeO2 particles act as nucleation sites during coating solidification.
CeO2-induced nucleation produces finer grains and more strongly pinned grain boundaries.
During high-temperature sliding, the CeO2-related sites facilitate formation and stabilization of a protective oxide tribo-layer.
The grain-boundary oxide films and protective tribo-layer impede dislocation motion.
The protective oxide tribo-layer suppresses microcrack initiation.
The nano-CeO2-modified coating will have a lower wear rate than the unmodified baseline.
The nano-CeO2-modified coating will exhibit less microscopic plastic deformation, including fewer microcracks and less plastic flow, than the baseline.
The predicted improvement is limited to high-temperature sliding in an oxidizing environment where tribo-oxidation contributes significantly to surface protection.
The magnitude of wear reduction and grain refinement depends on CeO2 content and processing parameters.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant wear-rate decrease together with similar or increased microscopic plastic deformation would falsify the hypothesis.
